key_insight: SCCL-DT reduces false-negative contrastive pairs in chest X-ray vision-language pretraining by using adaptive, semantic-conflict-aware masking and distilling two teacher rules into one student model.
clinical_relevance: The approach aims to improve zero-shot chest X-ray diagnosis, potentially making AI systems more reliable across diverse patient reports and findings.
method: Tracks image-report similarity with EMA statistics to set adaptive thresholds.
Hard-masks suspected semantic-conflict pairs before softmax contrastive learning.
Distills two teachers built from inclusive (OR) and consensus (AND) rules into one deployable student.
evidence_signal: On five public chest X-ray benchmarks, the method reached a mean zero-shot AUC of 0.850 versus 0.837 for the strongest baseline reported in the abstract.
watch_item: The masking and thresholding depend on evolving similarity distributions, so performance may be sensitive to domain shift and calibration in new datasets.
paper_title: SCCL-DT: Semantic-Conflict-Aware Contrastive Learning with Dual-Rule Teacher Distillation for Zero-Shot Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
